- Scrolling up past the header clips row by row (row 0 hides first, rows 1+2 remain)

title: LCARS nvim terminal frame
description:
Build a live nvim-native LCARS-framed terminal — a replacement for the standard :terminal that renders each shell command's output inside LCARS chrome (elbow PNG header, periwinkle bar, chip pills, stem column, hcap footer), with a sticky orange-stem input buffer at the bottom.

- Custom nvim buffer (not :terminal) + jobstart(pty=true)
- OSC 133 A/B/C/D marks parsed from raw PTY bytes → block lifecycle events
- baleia.nvim for ANSI SGR → extmarks
- Unicode placeholder protocol for elbow/hcap PNGs (scroll with content)
- Separate term_input.lua for the input panel (command_buffer.lua untouched)

| live    | sage              |
| done    | periwinkle        |
| failed  | red               |

  block_record.lua     — A→D data model
  image_registry.lua   — PNG transmit + kitty image ID cache
  frame_renderer.lua   — pure render: header/content/footer into buffer
  frame_buffer.lua     — display buffer owner; append/update blocks
  pty_session.lua      — PTY job + OSC 133 parser + carry-buffer
  term_input.lua       — orange-stem input panel, chansend submit

comments.author: Seth Woodworth
comments.text:
Implemented terminal_win.lua per the wiring-notes contract, plus the three
resolved scope calls: :LcarsTerm reuses an existing session instead of
opening a second one; pty_session.start() is sized from the real display
window's width/height (resize-on-VimResized stays deferred to qm0.5);

While verifying against a real shell, found and fixed three pre-existing
bugs blocking end-to-end verification (all upstream of this bead's own
file, in the already-closed lcarcat-unk):

1. pty_session.lua's on_stdout never flushed a line. nvim's on_stdout
   already splits the raw byte stream on "\n" before the callback sees
   `data`, but _parse_chunk expects to find literal \n bytes itself to

   the prompt's own chrome (swoop bar, STARDATE line) is dropped rather
   than leaking into captured command output (relies on the same
   skip_lines window pty_session already uses for echoed input, plus the
   fact that no block is open between D and A).
3. A trailing \r held in carry across a chunk boundary could leak into
   emitted line text as a literal ^M when the flush was triggered by a
   bare \n or an OSC start rather than the paired \r\n case. Fixed with a

passing) and a new integration test (test/integration/terminal_win.sh)

title: term-input: orange-stem input panel submitting to PTY
description:
Create nvim/lua/lcars/term_input.lua

New file — does NOT touch command_buffer.lua (preserved for kitty send-text workflow).

Orange-stem input panel (same visual as command_buffer.lua but submits to PTY).

API:
  M.open(pty_session) → creates fixed-height split below display, applies winhighlight
  M.submit() → calls pty_session.send(buf_contents)

Reuse patterns from command_buffer.lua:
  - winhighlight for LcarsCmdStem / LcarsCmdStemDim
  - signcolumn=yes:1
  - Telescope history search
  - resize() debounce on TextChanged

Key difference from command_buffer.lua: submit() uses pty_session.send() not kitty @ send-text.
design:
RESOLVED API (supersedes original description and the 2026-08-25 comment):

M.open(buf, opts) — opts = { win, on_submit, min_height = 4, max_height = 10 }
  - buf/win are created by the caller (terminal_win.lua, or a test harness
    standing in for it) — term_input.lua does NOT call nvim_open_win itself.
  - opts.on_submit(cmd_text) is a plain callback. term_input never requires
    pty_session or terminal_win by name.
  - In the real system, terminal_win.lua passes a wrapper as on_submit that
    sets rec.command = cmd_text THEN calls pty_session.send(cmd_text) — this
    is how rec.command gets set before the PTY executes (the concern the
    2026-08-25 comment raised). block_record is owned entirely by
    terminal_win.lua; term_input.lua never references it.
  - Before terminal_win.lua (lcarcat-2z9) exists, a test script can stand in
    for it: create the split/buffer itself, pass
    on_submit = pty_session.send directly. Proves the input->PTY path works
    end-to-end (real shell execution) with no framed display yet.

M.submit() — reads buf, strips trailing blanks, joins lines with \n, calls
  opts.on_submit(text), then CLEARS the buffer to a single blank line
  (fresh-prompt UX — differs from command_buffer.lua, which leaves submitted
  text in place).

Keymap convention same as command_buffer.lua: multi-line buffer, normal-mode
<CR> submits, insert-mode <CR> inserts a newline.

New highlight groups (not LcarsCmdStem*, to avoid sharing global state with
the kitty-pane command buffer): LcarsTermInputStem, LcarsTermInputStemDim,
LcarsTermInputCursorNr, LcarsTermInputCursorLine.
notes:
Verified end-to-end via test/integration/term_input.sh (LCARCAT_SKIP_SCREENSHOTS=1):
PASS — a command typed into the input buffer and submitted via normal-mode
<CR> reaches a real PTY shell and executes (marker-file assertion).

Two bugs found and fixed during verification, both in the TEST fixture, not
in term_input.lua itself:
1. test/integration/term_input_test.lua originally called
   vim.cmd('startinsert') at the end of the :luafile execution — this
   doesn't stick (nvim reverts to Normal mode when the outer ex-command
   returns), and even deferring via vim.schedule left the buffer in
   Insert mode by the time the script's own nvim_check_messages ran its
   `:redir ... | messages` Ex command, which then got typed as literal
   text into the input buffer instead of executing. Fixed by not having
   the fixture touch insert mode at all — the driving shell script already
   sends its own explicit Esc+i before typing, which is deterministic.
2. The shared _nvim_focused_window_id helper (is_focused-based) returns
   nothing when kitty is launched from a background/non-interactive
   session — the window never receives real OS focus. term_input.sh
   resolves the window by id directly instead (there's only ever one).

Known environment limitation, not a code bug: live screenshot capture
(screencapture -l<id>) is unreliable in this background-job context —
"could not create image from window" even after Screen Recording
permission was granted, likely because an unfocused fullscreen window
isn't actually composited. test/integration/term_input.sh still captures
screenshots by default (LCARCAT_SKIP_SCREENSHOTS=1 to skip) — run it
interactively for the visual check (orange stem, buffer clears on submit).

title: pty-session: PTY job + OSC 133 parser + line carry-buffer
description:
Create nvim/lua/lcars/pty_session.lua

jobstart(shell, {pty=true}). This is the riskiest primitive — bytes arrive in chunks, not complete lines.

Responsibilities:
- Carry-buffer for incomplete escape sequences across on_stdout chunks
- Line splitter: split on \r\n, carry partial last line
- OSC 133 state machine:
    \x1b]133;A → on_prompt_start()
    \x1b]133;B → on_command_start(command_text)
    \x1b]133;C → on_command_exec()
    \x1b]133;D;N → on_command_done(exit_code)
- Everything else (non-OSC bytes) forwarded to on_output_line(line) callback
- M.send(text) → chansend(job_id, text .. '\n')

API:
  M.start(shell_cmd, callbacks) → starts PTY job
  M.send(text) → writes to PTY stdin
  M.stop() → jobstop
notes: Schema note (from b3r): block_record now includes command_start and command_end (epoch seconds) alongside duration (derived). pty_session must set rec.command_start at OSC 133;B and rec.command_end + rec.duration at OSC 133;D. duration = command_end - command_start. All three fields are nil in block_record.new().

title: spike-1: Unicode placeholder transmission from Lua
description:
Verify that image.nvim from_file() places an elbow PNG in a scratch buffer and scrolls correctly with the buffer via WinScrolled re-render.

FINDINGS:

What works:
- image.nvim from_file() with window+buffer+x/y binding renders immediately (no scroll required)
- WinScrolled re-render is handled by image.nvim's global autocmd — no manual hook needed
- io.write(apc_escape) transmission works from Lua; asset path, cell dims, and base64 all function correctly

- Unicode placeholder via extmark/highlight: termguicolors=true forces nvim to emit \e[38;2;r;g;b;m always; kitty needs \e[38;5;<id>m — incompatible, extmarks cannot carry the image ID

title: Planet position widget using astropy
description:
Implement a kitty page widget that displays current planet positions (azimuth, altitude, constellation) for the observer's location.

Reference implementation: https://leancrew.com/all-this/2026/08/a-planet-position-widget/

The script uses astropy to query positions for Moon, Sun, Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn relative to a fixed observer location (lat=41.81433, lon=-88.07093, height=208m).

Output columns per planet: name, azimuth (degrees), compass direction, altitude (degrees), constellation.

Implementation notes:
- Base the widget on the example script from the reference URL above — document that source in code comments
- Observer location is from the reference script; make it configurable or document how to change it
- Display should integrate with lcarcat frame/chip/pill rendering
- Original script piped output to TerminalWidget.app; replace that with lcarcat display primitives
design:
Built WITHOUT astropy, deliberately, after measuring both options.

MEASURED: astropy import = 3.77 s on this machine; 0.35 s to query 9 bodies. The dashboard redraws on a timer, so a 3.8 s import is paid before the first frame ever appears. The self-contained implementation (dashboard/sources/ephemeris.py) imports in microseconds — only math and datetime.

Methods used, both published: JPL 'Approximate Positions of the Planets' (Keplerian elements at J2000 + linear rates, then Kepler's equation) for the planets; Meeus Astronomical Algorithms ch.47 truncated series for the moon.

CROSS-VALIDATED AGAINST ASTROPY at three dates spanning 2025-2027:
  sun      worst  0.6 arcmin
  planets  worst  5.0 arcmin (Saturn); most under 1 arcmin
  moon     worst 56   arcmin (~0.94 deg, ~2 lunar diameters)
Distance errors: planets <=0.006 AU (Uranus), sun 0.00005 AU, moon 0.00004 AU.

The moon is the weak one and that is inherent to a truncated series. Acceptable because nothing displayed depends on better: the phase disc, illuminated fraction, and above/below horizon all survive a degree. NOT suitable for placing the moon among stars.

This accuracy is now a test rather than a claim — EphemerisAccuracyTest in test/unit/dashboard_test.py asserts the per-body tolerances against astropy and SKIPS when astropy is absent, so the dashboard stays testable without it:
    uv run --with astropy python test/unit/dashboard_test.py

REVISIT IF: someone wants rise/set times, precise conjunction timing, or the moon placed against a star field. Seth confirmed dependencies are acceptable, so astropy remains available as an opt-in source behind the same SkyPosition interface if the requirement changes.
close_reason: Delivered as OrreryWidget + SkyWidget + MoonWidget over a self-contained ephemeris, cross-validated against astropy. astropy itself rejected on a measured 3.8s import cost; decision and accuracy figures recorded in the design field.

title: Verify context discipline: monitor context growth during Tab A resume session
description:
Meta-task attached to the Tab A resume work. The context-discipline changes from 2026-08-14 (visual-inspector subagent, grid-inspector subagent, offset/limit read discipline, docs/block_demo split) need real-world validation on an actual working session before we treat them as proven.

## Instructions for the session that picks up 2m7.10.1

Throughout the session, self-monitor for these anti-patterns and note them:

1. Any `Read` of a PNG in the main loop → should have been delegated to `visual-inspector`.
2. Any `Read` of `nvim/lua/lcars/block_demo.lua` without `offset`/`limit` → should have grepped first, then read a bounded window.
3. Any `Read` of an observation file for a tab you weren't working on → the point of the split was to avoid this.
4. Any full `test/get_cell_grid.py --dump-grid` output in main context → should have been delegated to `grid-inspector`.
5. Any re-read of a file immediately after `Edit` → the tool harness tracks state; re-read is wasted tokens.

## What to report at session close
- Rough context percentage at session start and at close (from `/context` if the user runs it).
- Any of the 5 anti-patterns above that slipped through, with a short note on why.
- Any subagent delegation that DIDN'T work well (e.g. subagent returned too much detail; parent had to re-derive).
- Suggested tweaks to AGENTS.md "Context discipline" section or the subagent instructions in `.claude/agents/`.

## What NOT to do
- Do not restructure the discipline rules mid-session on your own; note issues and let the user decide.
- Do not skip the subagents "for speed" — the discipline is the point.

Close this bead only when the session that picks up 2m7.10.1 (right cap regression) has completed a full loop (deploy, capture, inspect, fix, verify) and the user has reviewed the context-usage report.

Anti-patterns from the watchlist: no PNGs read in main loop (visual-inspector used throughout); no unbounded block_demo.lua reads (grepped first, Read with offset/limit); no cross-tab observation reads; no full get_cell_grid.py --dump-grid in main context (grid-inspector used); no post-Edit re-reads. Delegation worked well overall. Meta-finding surfaced during the session: deploy.sh is the missing step — ~/.config/nvim/lua/lcars/block_demo.lua is a copy, not a symlink, so edits do not reach the running nvim until ./deploy.sh runs. description:
New script test/overlay_grid.py that annotates a screenshot PNG with a cell-boundary grid and col/row numbers.

AFFECTED BY qm0.9 (2026-08-28) — read before starting.

The prompt is now two files, and hook ordering is load-bearing. Do NOT
`add-zsh-hook precmd atuin_precmd` and hope for the best; the current order is
installed as a unit by lcars_prompt_data_install:

  precmd_functions  = (_lcars_data_precmd_open  _lcars_swoop_precmd  _lcars_data_precmd_close)
  preexec_functions = (_lcars_swoop_preexec     _lcars_data_preexec)

The constraints that make it an order rather than a list:
  - _lcars_data_precmd_open emits OSC 133;D FIRST, before any decorative output,
    so whatever prints next streams out while no block is open.
  - _lcars_data_precmd_close emits 133;A/chips/OSC 7/133;B LAST. B opens the
    skip_lines suppression window that hides the prompt's own bytes from the
    next command's captured output.
  - _lcars_data_preexec emits 133;C LAST, closing that window.

So: an atuin hook that PRINTS must land in the renderer slot (between open and
close). One that only records — which atuin's precmd is — can go before open or
after close, but NOT between close and the command, or its output would be
captured into the block.

Atuin's preexec must not land after _lcars_data_preexec, or anything it emits
lands inside the suppression window.

Simplest correct approach: extend lcars_prompt_data_install to accept the extra
hooks, rather than bolting add-zsh-hook calls on afterwards. That keeps the
ordering stated in one place, which is the whole point of the argument list.

Validation to add to this bead's existing criteria: after wiring atuin, confirm
in :LcarsTerm (not just kitty) that command blocks still open/close correctly and
that no atuin output leaks into a block's captured output. A kitty-only check
will not catch an ordering mistake — that is the failure mode qm0.9 existed to
remove.

title: nvim: periwinkle gutter continues to EOW and merges with statusline elbow
description:
## Goal

The gutter (line-number column) should remain periwinkle (#9999ff) all the way to the bottom of the nvim window, even when the file has fewer lines than the window height. Currently the gutter goes black below the last line of content.

At the bottom of the gutter, the periwinkle stem should merge into the statusline via an LCARS elbow swoop — the same style as the top-left corner chrome.

## Confirmed root cause

nvim 0.12.2 does **not** evaluate the `statuscolumn` expression for EOB (below-end-of-buffer) virtual rows. Confirmed empirically: setting `statuscolumn=%#LineNr#%{v:virtnum}` shows the value on real lines but the cells for EOB rows remain blank/black — the expression is never called.

`winhighlight=EndOfBuffer:SignColumn` does paint the gutter periwinkle on EOB rows but bleeds the color across the full row width (text area included). Not usable.

statuscol.nvim was evaluated and also cannot fix this — its per-segment `hl` wrapping depends on the same `statuscolumn` evaluation path that nvim skips for EOB rows.

## Design: floating window fill

A `style="minimal"` floating window positioned over exactly the EOB gutter cells:

```lua
nvim_open_win(buf, false, {
  relative = "win",
  row      = wi.botline,      -- first row below last line of content
  col      = 0,
  width    = wi.textoff,      -- exact gutter column count
  height   = wi.height - wi.botline,
  style    = "minimal",
  focusable = false,
})
-- then:  vim.wo[win].winhighlight = "Normal:SignColumn"
```

Confirmed working in the test harness: col 0–3 periwinkle on all EOB rows, col 4+ (text area) stays black.

### Events

Four autocmds, each doing one `getwininfo()` call + one `nvim_win_set_config()` (or open/close):

- `BufEnter`, `WinEnter` — buffer or focus change may change botline/textoff
- `WinResized` — window height changed
- `WinScrolled` — user scrolled; botline changes

Logic per event:
```
wi = getwininfo(current_win)
eob_rows = wi.height - wi.botline
if eob_rows <= 0 → close float (file fills window)
else → resize/reposition float to correct geometry
```

The debounce pattern already used in chrome.lua applies here too.

### Integration with chrome.lua

The bottom-left elbow image already placed by chrome.lua sits at `y = statusline_row - 1`. The EOB fill float sits above that. They don't overlap as long as the file has at least one EOB row above the elbow. No coordination needed beyond existing chrome refresh.

## Cleanup required before implementation

- **Remove statuscol.nvim** from `~/.config/nvim/lua/plugins.lua` (was added directly to personal lazy config during this investigation — not from the lcarcat repo)
- **Remove `nvim/lua/lcars/statuscolumn.lua`** from the repo (the statuscol.nvim wrapper is no longer the approach)
- **Revert `nvim/colors/lcars.lua`** — restore the hand-written `statuscolumn` line (or remove it; the float approach doesn't depend on it)

## Acceptance criteria

1. Open `test/fixtures/short_file.py` in a full-height nvim window
2. `get_cell_grid.py --col 0 --expect-bg periwinkle` passes for all rows above the statusline
3. `get_cell_grid.py --col 4 --skip-rows 11 --expect-bg black` passes (text area stays black)
4. A bottom-left elbow swoop image is placed at the join of the gutter stem and statusline (existing chrome.lua behavior)

## Test

```bash
bash test/scenarios/nvim_eob_gutter.sh
```

title: zsh prompt: first bg cell misaligned with elbow stem by one pixel
description: The leftmost background cell in the zsh prompt does not line up with the elbow stem — there is a one-pixel gap or overlap. Fix candidate: make PROMPT2 use a placeholder cell (grid row 2, col 0) instead of a plain %K cell, so both input lines use the same image rendering path.

title: Screenshot harness leaks kitty/nvim processes on scenario exit
description:
The screenshot test harness leaves processes running after a scenario finishes:

- The dedicated test kitty instance (--title=LCARCAT-TEST) survives.
- nvim command-buffer and vsplit processes inside it survive.
- The unix socket at /tmp/lcarcat-test.sock may or may not be cleaned up.

Design intent: running a scenario should be self-contained. When the scenario script exits (normally, on error, or on interrupt), no processes it launched should remain, and the socket should be gone. Currently vsplit_nvim_command_buffer.sh explicitly skips teardown 'to preserve screenshots for manual review', but the screenshots are files on disk — the live kitty and nvim processes do not need to be preserved for that. Even scenarios that do call teardown rely on kitty @ close-window succeeding on a live socket; if the harness aborts before teardown, processes leak.

Observed leftovers include nvim instances still running the command_buffer lua module hours/days after a scenario ran.

Acceptance:
- Running any scenario in test/scenarios/ leaves no LCARCAT-TEST kitty process, no nvim child of it, and no /tmp/lcarcat-test.sock after the script exits — including on error/interrupt.
- Screenshots in /tmp/lcarcat-screenshots/ are still preserved.
close_reason: Harness teardown now closes all windows, force-kills the tracked kitty pid if it survives close-window, and removes socket + pidfile. Scenarios install trap teardown EXIT INT TERM so cleanup runs on normal exit, error, or Ctrl-C. Verified end-to-end: no kitty/nvim leaks after normal exit or mid-run SIGINT; screenshots preserved. LCARCAT_KEEP_ALIVE=1 opt-in preserves the live kitty for manual inspection.

title: Kitty pane separator renders as a 1-pixel hairline
description: The border between kitty panes renders as a single physical pixel — orange when active, periwinkle when inactive. At this width the separator reads as a hairline rather than a structural LCARS stem. LCARS pane separators should carry enough visual weight to be immediately readable as structural elements.
notes:
MEASURED 2026-09-11, see lcarcat-qbg: kitty panes do NOT share a cell lattice.
Adjacent panes have independent grid origins and the space between them is a
sub-cell pixel gap that varies with window size (measured 10px / 15px / 20px at
os-window widths 1700 / 1705 / 1710, with pane-2 lattice offsets of 9px / 14px /
0px against a 19px cell). The stacked case is the same: 21px gap, 21px offset of
a 38px row.

This kills BOTH previous recommendations on this bead:
 - the 2026-09-01 note ("border becomes a 1-cell periwinkle rail") is not
   expressible -- there is no cell to fill, only a variable sliver;
 - the 2026-09-02 note ("black at roughly a cell's width") is closer but still
   describes the gap as if it had a stable cell width. It does not.

What this bug actually is, restated: the separator reads as a hairline because
kitty draws a ~1px border line inside an otherwise-black variable gap. The
levers are window_border_width (pixels, not cells) and the border colors. Any
target weight must be chosen in PIXELS and will never align to either pane's
grid, so it cannot carry a cell-based LCARS shape -- no elbow, no cap, no stem
can live in that gap. It can only be a plain line or plain black.

Also still true and worth fixing regardless: inactive_border_color is #9999cc
where the palette's periwinkle is #9999ff.

title: overlay_grid / crop_grid: resolve cells per kitty pane
description:
Make the pixel->cell tools pane-aware instead of assuming one global lattice.

WHY: measured 2026-09-11 (lcarcat-qbg) — adjacent kitty panes do NOT share a
cell lattice. kitty gives each pane a whole number of cells, then splits the
leftover sub-cell pixels roughly half into the inter-pane gap and half to the far
edge, so every pane but the top-left one has its own origin offset by a fraction
of a cell (9px and 14px of a 19px cell, at window widths 10px apart). Today
overlay_grid.py and crop_grid.py draw ONE lattice over the whole screenshot, so a
split capture is mislabelled everywhere except the first pane, silently, with
grid lines cutting through glyphs rather than between them.

Documented as a hard limit for now — see docs/test-tools.md "The one-lattice
assumption", the AGENTS.md invariant, the tool docstrings, and the
visual-inspector agent brief (lcarcat-duw covered that write-up). This bead is
the actual fix.

SCOPE:
 1. Teach overlay_grid.py a --socket/--window mode: ask kitty for the tab's
    window list, derive each pane's pixel rect, and draw a SEPARATE lattice per
    pane with per-pane origins and its own col/row numbering (labels want a pane
    id so "col 7" is unambiguous — e.g. "w3:c7").
 2. Same for crop_grid.py: --window N should make --col/--row relative to THAT
    pane's grid.
 3. GUARD FIRST, and worth landing on its own even if the rest waits: when a
    socket is available and the captured tab reports more than one window,
    refuse (or loudly warn) rather than drawing a misleading grid. The silent
    wrongness is the actual danger, not the missing feature.

THE HARD PART is deriving each pane's pixel origin. `kitty @ ls` reports columns
and lines per window but NOT pixel geometry, so the origin has to be either
computed from kitty's own layout arithmetic (fragile, version-dependent) or
measured. A measurement path already exists and is reliable: fill each pane with
a distinct solid colour and take its bounding box — that is exactly how qbg was
measured, and it could be packaged as a one-shot `--calibrate` that writes a
pane->origin map for the current layout, then reused across captures until the
layout changes.

Relates to lcarcat-1la (deriving cell size via CSI 16t / --socket) — both are
"stop hardcoding capture geometry, ask the terminal", and they likely want the
same --socket plumbing.

NOT URGENT: no current caller needs it. Every overlay_grid/crop_grid user runs
against a single fullscreen pane, and the one split-creating flow
(test/integration/cmd_buffer_target_pane.sh) asserts via get-text only. This
becomes real when someone wants pixel assertions on a multi-pane layout — most
likely the kitty half of lcarcat-cg7.

title: docs: rule 4 (no T/+ junctions) is scoped too broadly
description:
docs/lcars-design.md rule 4 says "No T/+ junctions. THIS IS THE DESIGN LAW",
and draws the consequence that "an elbow at every window corner is wrong for
nvim ... use the outer-frame-only model instead".

The reference panel Seth supplied on 2026-09-02
(lcars-example-holodeck-programming.jpg, repo root) shows canonical LCARS
letting four frames meet flush at a crossing, with square inner corners and no
break. So the rule is about a BAR RUNNING INTO A STEM -- which does need an
elbow or a cap -- not about a FRAME MEETING A FRAME, which may simply meet.

title: visual-inspector reported a false defect from stale cell-size constants
description:
The visual-inspector agent definition asserted cellw=38/cellh=76 as 'fixed geometry — never recalculate', and explicitly forbade deriving cell size from pixel math. Every PNG in test/screenshots/ is actually 19x38 px per cell (1x capture, not 2x HiDPI), which is also crop_grid.py's default.

Consequence: during lcarcat-ba0 the agent measured an 8-cell chip as 4 cells and reported a correctly-rendered footer gap as missing. Nearly caused a fix to already-correct code.

Fixed in .claude/agents/visual-inspector.md: constants corrected to 19x38, reframed as 'typical, verify per image', with a procedure for deriving px/cell from a known-width element and a requirement to state the cell size used when an answer turns on exact columns.

Remaining question (why this bead exists): why did the doc say 38x76? Likely written when captures were 2x HiDPI (different display or font size). If capture geometry can legitimately vary by machine, the constants should not be in prose at all — screenshot_harness.sh should emit the cell size alongside each PNG (a sidecar or filename suffix), the way the asset pipeline already encodes 19x38pixels in asset filenames.
notes:
FIX CONFIRMED WORKING, plus a different failure class, 2026-08-31.

The 19x38 correction holds up. Across ~6 visual-inspector delegations this
session the agent stated the cell size it used and verified it per image
("Confirmed cell geometry by direct pixel scan (not assumed)"), and correctly
found no elbow seam where there was none — the opposite of the ba0 false
positive that prompted this bead. Geometry side looks solved.

A DIFFERENT failure showed up though, and it is not about constants:

Shooting README screenshots, the inspector twice misattributed pane CONTENT. It
reported the left pane as "neovim showing vim help/documentation" when the pane
was actually a zsh shell with `less` open on its help screen, and read a kitty
tab title as evidence that the left pane was running nvim. Both readings were
confident and both were wrong; they sent me chasing an nvim swap-file theory for
one round.

What settled it in one call was not another screenshot:
    kitty @ --to $SOCK ls          -> real window/cmdline/geometry mapping
    kitty @ --to $SOCK get-text --match id:N   -> the pane's actual text
That showed win 1 running /bin/zsh with less's JUMPING/marks help in its buffer,
which immediately identified the real cause (shot 07 leaves a pager open; the
`h` in "ls -lh demos/" opens less help).

Suggested amendment to .claude/agents/visual-inspector.md: state that the agent
answers RENDERING questions (alignment, seams, color, clipping, banding) and
that CONTENT questions — what program is running, what a pane is showing, what
text is present — should be answered with `kitty @ get-text` / `kitty @ ls`
against the live session, which is both ground truth and far cheaper. Guessing
which program produced text from its pixels is not a reliable operation.

title: frame.lua: extract block frame primitives from block_demo.lua
description:
Extract reusable frame-building primitives from nvim/lua/lcars/block_demo.lua into a new module nvim/lua/lcars/frame.lua. The goal is a clean three-layer API:

- append_* functions: pure Lua table manipulation, no nvim API — append rows to a shared lines table and return the start row index. These build text strings only; no highlights, no images.
- annotate_* functions: called after buf_set_lines, apply extmarks and highlight groups to a buffer. Take buf + namespace + row anchors as arguments.
- image_specs_* functions: pure path/coordinate math — return tables of {path, dx, dy, w, h} for callers to pass to image.nvim. No image.nvim calls here.

Also include: find_asset_dir (asset directory selection probing for both elbow and corner), elbow_path / corner_path / hcap_path (filename builders), setup_hls (idempotent highlight group registration).

After extraction, block_demo.lua becomes a thin orchestrator: calls frame.* in order, collects specs, writes lines, runs annotations, places images. Tab and window management stays in block_demo.

Open questions to answer before/during this session:
- Is there a case where you'd mix elbow header with corner footer (or vice versa)? What determines which to use — block height, visual style, content type?
- Should image_specs_* return specs or should they place images directly? (direct placement couples frame.lua to image.nvim; returning specs keeps it decoupled but requires callers to know image.nvim API)
- What is the right namespace strategy — one global ns per session, or one per block instance?

The recent visual-regression work on 2m7.10 (Tab A stem alignment, chip gaps, cap regression at 2m7.10.1, and 6 remaining per-tab beads at 2m7.10.3-9) makes this split significantly more attractive than when originally filed:

title: block_demo.lua: fix TabEnter ghost images and render_all() tab navigation
description:
Two known bugs in nvim/lua/lcars/block_demo.lua from the block demo session:

1. Ghost images on tab switch: windowless images are pinned to screen coordinates. Switching tabs leaves the previous tab's images visible until the new tab re-renders. TabEnter autocmd with vim.schedule(render) was added but the timing vs the next screenshot is tight — sometimes ghosts still appear. Root cause unknown: may need a longer delay, an explicit img:clear() sweep before re-render, or a different signal than TabEnter.

2. render_all() tab navigation: after rendering all tabs, the code navigates back to tab A via a bufname search. Under some conditions it lands on the wrong tab. The logic iterates nvim_list_tabpages() and looks for a buffer whose name matches 'lcars://demo/A-'. Root cause: bufname search may match a tab other than the first, or the list order is not guaranteed. Should use index 1 of nvim_list_tabpages() instead of string matching.

title: Unit tests for nvim and zsh
description:
## Goal

Headless unit tests for nvim configuration and zsh prompt logic — no running kitty or display required.

## Motivation

All current testing is scenario-based (kitty harness + live socket). This is slow, requires a display, and cannot run in CI. Well-specified behaviors — highlight groups, window geometry, float placement, prompt rendering — should have lightweight assertions that are fast and repeatable.

## Scope

title: Evaluate vim.ui.img as the windowless placement backend
description:
nvim 0.13 ships vim.ui.img (runtime/lua/vim/ui/img.lua + ui/img/_kitty.lua), an experimental built-in kitty-graphics API. Evaluated 2026-09-01 against image.nvim; this bead is the actionable residue.

It is a PRIMITIVE, not a replacement for image.nvim. ~200 lines: transmit PNG bytes (t=d, base64 in 4KB chunks) and place at absolute screen cells via a cursor move to CSI row;colH. No window/buffer binding, no scroll following, no Unicode-placeholder path, and no transmission dedupe — every set(bytes, opts) re-transmits. image.nvim remains required for anything buffer-bound.

WHY IT STILL MATTERS HERE: it is almost exactly the windowless absolute-screen address that lcarcat-05h.1 is inventing for chrome.lua. Upstream, maintained, and it sidesteps the render_offset_top = -1 workaround (an off-by-one in image.nvim's buffer-bound renderer that a windowless backend never hits).

Three capabilities image.nvim lacks:
 1. Per-image z-index. image.nvim hardcodes display_zindex = -1 (backends/kitty/init.lua:108), not exposed. vim.ui.img passes opts.zindex through as z=. In kitty, z < -1073741824 draws BELOW the cell background.
 2. Flicker-free move: set(id, {row, col}) reuses both img_id and placement_id, so kitty relocates an existing placement. chrome.lua currently clears and re-places on every layout event — same shape as lcarcat-fvv.
 3. A real capability handshake: _supported() does an APC round-trip via vim.tty.query_apc with a timeout, and special-cases Apple_Terminal. We currently gate on pcall(require, 'image').

SEPARABLE SPIKE, testable today without nvim 0.13 by dropping to raw APC: does a z-index below the cell background remove the need for alternate_screen.lua's suspend_chrome()/resume_chrome()? That pair exists only because kitty composites chrome images over the alternate-screen float and image.nvim cannot express 'draw me under an opaque window'. If z works, it deletes code rather than adding it. Depends on the float actually painting an opaque background — unverified.
design:
Do NOT switch wholesale, and do not take a hard dependency on nvim HEAD.

Target shape: image_registry keeps both placement addresses and its dedupe cache, and dispatches the WINDOWLESS address to vim.ui.img where available, falling back to image.nvim's absolute path otherwise. Buffer-bound placements stay on image.nvim regardless — it owns WinScrolled (init.lua:342), WinResized/WinNew (:351) and BufLeave/WinClosed/TabEnter (:296), which is what makes frame images scroll and hide with content (see lcarcat-382).

The dedupe must stay in OUR layer whichever backend is used: lcarcat places the same few elbow/cap PNGs repeatedly — per block header and footer today, per pane edge after lcarcat-05h.5 — and vim.ui.img would re-transmit the bytes every time. image.nvim caches by id + preprocessing hash (backends/kitty/init.lua:19-20, 68-76); vim.ui.img has no equivalent.

lcarcat-05h.1's two-address design is what makes this a backend swap rather than a rewrite. Worth keeping in mind while building it even though both addresses will initially go to image.nvim.
acceptance_criteria: Either the windowless address dispatches to vim.ui.img behind a capability check with image.nvim as fallback and no regression in chrome rendering, or the evaluation concludes it is not worth the branch and that conclusion is recorded here with its reasons.

Its semantics are not yet finalized.' Unblock when Seth upgrades to 0.13+ locally — and re-read img.lua at that point, because the semantics may well have moved.

The alternate_screen z-index spike described above is the exception: it needs no version upgrade and can be run any time.
